chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Qāsānī, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Minqarī, from Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
In the intimate discourse of Mūsā عليه السلام:
O Mūsā, when you see poverty approaching, then say: ‘Welcome to the emblem of the righteous’; and when you see wealth approaching, then say: ‘A sin whose punishment has been hastened.’

key_terms.بِشِعَارِ: as the emblem, sign, or distinguishing mark
key_terms.مُنَاجَاةِ: intimate divine discourse or whispered communion

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith teach believers to view poverty and wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith presents an ethical teaching expressed in the form of Allah’s intimate discourse to Mūsā عليه السلام. It praises poverty as a mark often associated with the righteous and warns against being deceived by worldly wealth, which may at times be a form of immediate requital.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Ali Bin Muhammad Al Qasany, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Bin Dawood Al Minqary, from Hafs Bin Giyas, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

“O Musa<sup>as</sup>! Whenever you see the poverty coming, so say: ‘Welcome to the banner of the righteous!’; and whenever you<sup>as</sup> see the riches coming, so say: ‘A sin, the Punishment of which has hastened’”’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari from Hafs ibn Ghiyath from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
It is in the conversation of Moses, ‘

O Moses, when you see poverty coming say, “Welcome to the way of life of the virtuous people. When, you see wealth coming, say, ‘It is a sin. I wanted to experience its punishment early (before the Day of Judgment).”’
